docs.title: UPanda
docs.text:
UPanda stands for: Ultrafast Parameter Analysis using Neural-accelerated Driven Algorithms

A Python library for rapid cosmological parameter inference using neural network-accelerated emulators. UPanda provides MCMC sampling capabilities with support for various cosmological likelihoods including CMB, LSS, and BAO data. The framework is designed to work with JAX for differentiable computations and supports both traditional TensorFlow/Keras emulators and JAX-based implementations.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fast MCMC sampling with multiple sampler options (emcee, nautilus, dynesty, ultranest)
  • Support for various cosmological likelihoods (Planck PR4/PR3, ACT DR4/DR6, Pantheon+, and a general likelihood class for LSS cross-correlations)
  • Neural network emulator integration for rapid theory predictions
  • JAX-compatible implementation for differentiable computations (vmap/jit compatible)
  • Flexible configuration via YAML files

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The best way to learn UPanda is through the working examples in the notebooks/ directory:

  • Planck PR4 with JAX - Full CMB analysis with neural emulators
  • DESI BAO DR2 - BAO parameter inference
  • Planck PR3 Tutorial - Complete MCMC walkthrough

See the Examples page for the full list of notebooks.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
pip install -e '.[dev]'
make style-check      # ruff
make test             # unit tests
make test-reference   # comparisons with reference likelihoods, see Validation
make docs             # documentation, built with MkDocs

The continuous integration runs the unit tests on Python 3.10 to 3.12 and the reference comparisons on 3.10. The documentation is published from master.

Several analysis codes import the likelihood classes directly, so please keep module paths, class names and constructor arguments as they are.

When adding a likelihood:

  • say in the module docstring where the data come from, and add a row to Data sources;
  • if cobaya or the collaboration provides a likelihood for the same data, add a comparison to tests/test_reference.py and a row to Validation;
  • check that it runs in both NumPy and JAX.

The data are read from src/UPanda/likelihoods/data/<directory>/. The small data sets are part of the repository; the others ("download" below) have to be placed in that directory by hand.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• eBOSS DR16 ELG likelihoods from the official SDSS files: the one-dimensional fσ8 table and the three-dimensional BAO + full-shape grid (eboss_elg), available through boss_dr16_fsigma8 and boss_dr16_rsd.
  • boss_dr16_fsigma8 uses the published SDSS covariance by default; additional_args={"diagonal": True} gives the previous behaviour. boss_dr16_rsd.drop_fsigma8() marginalises fσ8 for distance-only analyses.
  • general_lss: act_lensing_range selects the ACT DR6 lensing bandpowers (all, baseline, extended).
  • run_mcmc (emcee): chains are written to an HDF5 file while running and can be resumed; walkers can be started from an existing chain.
  • camspec_pr4: the covariance is inverted with NumPy, which removes a 40 minute JAX compilation on CPU.
  • Tests against cobaya on the real data for DESI, SDSS, Pantheon+, Union3, DES-Dovekie, Planck 2018 plik-lite and lensing, and against pyactlike for ACT DR4 (see Validation).

docs.title: 0.2.0 (September 2026)
docs.text:
• New likelihoods: Union3 and Union3.1, BOSS DR12 + eBOSS DR16 BAO and RSD.
  • ACT DR6 lensing: corrected the contraction of the N1 correction and the multipole indexing of the fiducial spectrum.
  • WMAP: corrected the off-diagonal Fisher matrices and the SZ template.
  • HiLLiPoP, LoLLiPoP and CamSpec: fixes to covariance compression, binning and the JAX code paths.
  • DES-Dovekie: redshift cuts now marginalise over the removed supernovae.
  • Sampling: consistent parameter ordering with fixed parameters and grouped Gaussian priors.

Some of these fixes change likelihood values with respect to 0.1.0.
First version: likelihoods, emulator classes (TensorFlow and JAX), samplers.

docs.title: Likelihood classes
docs.text:
Each likelihood is a class in its own module, with a lower-case name:

from UPanda.likelihoods.desi_bao_dr2 import desi_bao_dr2

The constructors share the arguments

  • emu_model_list: the emulators that provide the theory. An emulator is any object with a predict(parameters) method, where parameters is a dictionary of arrays; IntegratedModel (TensorFlow) and integrated_model_jax.IntegratedModel (JAX) are the classes shipped with UPanda, and both have restore(filename).
  • dtype: a structured NumPy dtype naming the sampled parameters, in the order of the columns of the array given to compute_like.
  • cosmology_params_fixed: a list of {"name": ..., "value": ...} for parameters that are held fixed.
  • additional_args: a dictionary of options specific to the likelihood.

compute_like(points) takes an array of shape (n_points, n_parameters) and returns one log-likelihood per point. Constant normalisation terms of the Gaussian likelihoods are left out.

Parameter conventions: omega_b and omega_cdm are physical densities (Ω h²), omega_m is Ω_m, and m_nu is the mass of one neutrino species in eV (three degenerate species are assumed).

docs.title: Supplying the theory directly
docs.text:
Instead of an emulator, the theory prediction can be set by hand and the likelihood evaluated with compute_like(None):

Likelihood set_external_spectra(...) Content desi_bao_dr2 {"desi_bao_data": vector} BAO distances in the order of mean.txt boss_dr16_rsd {"boss_dr16_rsd_data": vector} in the order of the attributes quantities and z_eff boss_dr16_fsigma8 {"boss_dr16_fsigma8_data": vector} fσ8 at z_eff pantheon_plus, union3, des_dovekie vector 5 log10[(1 + z_hel)(1 + z_cmb) D_A / Mpc] at the attribute zcmb camspec_pr4, hillipop {"tt": ..., "te": ..., "ee": ...} C_ℓ in K², from ℓ = 0 general_lss list of arrays one per emulator, same layout as the emulator outputs

A single vector gives a scalar; a two-dimensional array gives one value per row. The supernova likelihoods marginalise analytically over a constant magnitude offset, so the normalisation of the distances does not matter. With an emulator, the supernova likelihoods expect angular-diameter distances in Mpc and apply the conversion above themselves.

docs.title: CMB spectra shared between likelihoods
docs.text: Provider.set_Cl stores CMB C_ℓ in μK² from ℓ = 0, and Provider.get_Cl returns them to the likelihoods that need them (for example the lensing likelihoods, for their CMB-dependent corrections). The CMB likelihood has to be evaluated before the likelihoods that read its spectra.

docs.title: NumPy or JAX
docs.text:
import jax
jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
from UPanda import config
config.set_jax_enabled(True)

Choose the backend before building likelihoods and emulators. After switching, build them again: arrays already stored in existing objects are not converted. The setting is global to the process.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text: UPanda.run_panda.run_mcmc runs a chain for a list of likelihoods and emulators, with sampler one of emcee, nautilus, ultranest, hmc, or the optimisers adam and anneal. Priors and starting points come from the YAML configuration (see configs/ for examples); a parameter without a distribution entry has a flat prior. point_check evaluates the posterior at given points without running a chain.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Where a public reference implementation exists, the UPanda likelihood is compared with it on the real data. The reference is evaluated for a given cosmology, UPanda receives the same theory prediction, and the two log-likelihoods are compared. For the cobaya comparisons the theory comes from CAMB through cobaya, at two ΛCDM cosmologies. ACT DR4 is evaluated on the two best-fit spectra distributed with pyactlike.

UPanda likelihood Reference Difference in ln L desi_bao_dr2 cobaya bao.desi_dr2.desi_bao_all < 1e-9 (relative) desi_bao_2024 cobaya bao.desi_2024_bao_all < 1e-9 (relative) boss_dr16_rsd, BOSS DR12 + eBOSS LRG cobaya bao.sdss_dr16_baoplus_lrg < 1e-8 boss_dr16_rsd, eBOSS QSO cobaya bao.sdss_dr16_baoplus_qso < 1e-8 boss_dr16_rsd, eBOSS ELG cobaya bao.sdss_dr16_baoplus_elg 0.03 to 0.04 pantheon_plus cobaya sn.pantheonplus < 1e-8 (relative) union3 (Union3) cobaya sn.union3 < 1e-8 (relative) des_dovekie cobaya sn.desdovekie < 1e-8 (relative) planck_2018_highell_lowell, high-ℓ part cobaya planck_2018_highl_plik.TTTEEE_lite_native < 1e-7 (relative) planck_2018_lensing cobaya planck_2018_lensing.CMBMarged < 1e-6 (relative) act_dr4 pyactlike 1e-4 lollipop planck-npipe/lollipop < 1e-11 (relative) camspec_pr4 cobaya CamSpec: foreground and calibration model only < 1e-13 (relative)

The eBOSS ELG likelihood is a tabulated, non-Gaussian likelihood on a grid in (D_M/r_d, D_H/r_d, fσ8). Both codes read the official grid; cobaya interpolates it linearly in ln L, while UPanda first smooths it by 0.7 grid cells to remove its sampling noise and then uses a cubic interpolation. The difference quoted above comes from that choice.

These tests are in tests/test_reference.py. To run them:

pip install cobaya camb
pip install 'planck_2020_lollipop @ git+https://github.com/planck-npipe/lollipop.git' \
    'pyactlike @ git+https://github.com/ACTCollaboration/pyactlike.git'
cobaya-install bao.desi_dr2.desi_bao_all bao.desi_2024_bao_all bao.sdss_dr16_baoplus_lrg \
    bao.sdss_dr16_baoplus_qso bao.sdss_dr16_baoplus_elg sn.pantheonplus sn.union3 sn.desdovekie \
    planck_2018_highl_plik.TTTEEE_lite_native planck_2018_lensing.CMBMarged -p <packages>
COBAYA_PACKAGES_PATH=<packages> make test-reference

A test is skipped if its reference code or data is missing. They also run in the continuous integration.

Two more comparisons need large data sets and are run by hand:

  • scripts/check_act_lensing_reference.py compares the ACT DR6 lensing bandpowers and likelihood with act_dr6_lenslike;
  • scripts/check_wmap_reference.py compares the WMAP TT and TE likelihood terms with pyWMAP.

docs.title: Not compared yet
docs.text: The following have unit tests but no end-to-end comparison with a reference code: hillipop and the full camspec_pr4 likelihood, act_dr6, planck_sroll2_lowell_ee, the compressed low-ℓ TT and EE terms of the Planck 2018 likelihoods, the ACT variants planck_2018_for_act and planck_2018_for_act_dr6, and the MGS block of boss_dr16_rsd. Union3.1 and boss_dr16_fsigma8 have no cobaya counterpart. general_lss takes its data vector and covariance from the user, so there is nothing to compare it with.

docs.title: UPanda.config
docs.text:
Configuration module for managing JAX/NumPy backend switching.

This module provides a simple interface to enable or disable JAX backend usage across the UPanda package. When JAX is enabled, operations use JAX arrays and functions for improved performance with JIT compilation and automatic differentiation.

Attributes: is_jax_enabled (bool): Global flag indicating whether JAX backend is currently enabled. Defaults to False.

docs.title: set_jax_enabled
docs.text:
set_jax_enabled(value: bool)

Enable or disable JAX backend globally.

This function sets the JAX backend flag and automatically reloads all UPanda modules that depend on the backend selection to ensure they pick up the correct numpy/jax functions.

Args: value (bool): True to enable JAX backend, False to use NumPy.

Source code in src/UPanda/config.py 
def set_jax_enabled(value: bool):
    """Enable or disable JAX backend globally.

    This function sets the JAX backend flag and automatically reloads
    all UPanda modules that depend on the backend selection to ensure
    they pick up the correct numpy/jax functions.

    Args:
        value (bool): True to enable JAX backend, False to use NumPy.
    """
    global is_jax_enabled
    old_value = is_jax_enabled
    is_jax_enabled = value

    # If the value changed, reload modules to pick up the new backend
    if old_value != value:
        try:
            _reload_modules()
        except Exception:
            is_jax_enabled = old_value
            _reload_modules()
            raise

docs.title: Integrated Model
docs.text: Neural network emulator integration for fast theory predictions.

docs.title: UPanda.integrated_model_jax
docs.text:
JAX-based integrated emulator models for cosmological predictions.

This module provides JAX/Flax-based implementations of integrated emulator models, enabling JIT compilation and automatic differentiation. It includes custom activation functions compatible with JAX transformations (vmap, jit).

The module provides utilities for converting TensorFlow models to JAX/Flax and for inserting zero columns in predictions (useful for masked spectra).

docs.title: MyNetwork
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Flax neural network module with custom activation functions.

This module implements a multi-layer neural network with custom activation functions in each hidden layer, matching the TensorFlow CustomActivation behavior but implemented in Flax for JAX compatibility.

Attributes: weights (list): List of (weight, bias) tuples for each layer. hyper_params (list): List of (alpha, beta) tuples for custom activations.

Source code in src/UPanda/integrated_model_jax.py 
class MyNetwork(nn.Module):
    """Flax neural network module with custom activation functions.

    This module implements a multi-layer neural network with custom activation
    functions in each hidden layer, matching the TensorFlow CustomActivation
    behavior but implemented in Flax for JAX compatibility.

    Attributes:
        weights (list): List of (weight, bias) tuples for each layer.
        hyper_params (list): List of (alpha, beta) tuples for custom activations.
    """

    weights: list  # List of (weight, bias) tuples for each layer
    hyper_params: list  # List of (alpha, beta) for each custom activation layer

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x):
        # Loop over layers except the last one
        for (w, b), (a, b_hyper) in zip(self.weights[:-1], self.hyper_params):
            x = CustomActivation_jax(a=a, b=b_hyper)(dot(x, w) + b)

        # Final layer (no activation)
        final_w, final_b = self.weights[-1]
        x = dot(x, final_w) + final_b
        return x

docs.title: CustomActivation_jax
docs.text:
Bases: Module

JAX-compatible custom activation function matching arXiv:2106.03846.

This activation function uses fixed hyperparameters alpha and beta to create a learnable activation: (β + sigmoid(αx) * (1 - β)) * x

This is the JAX/Flax version of CustomActivation, designed to work with JAX transformations like vmap and jit.

Attributes: a (float): Alpha hyperparameter. b (float): Beta hyperparameter.

Source code in src/UPanda/integrated_model_jax.py 
class CustomActivation_jax(nn.Module):
    """JAX-compatible custom activation function matching arXiv:2106.03846.

    This activation function uses fixed hyperparameters alpha and beta to
    create a learnable activation: (β + sigmoid(αx) * (1 - β)) * x

    This is the JAX/Flax version of CustomActivation, designed to work with
    JAX transformations like vmap and jit.

    Attributes:
        a (float): Alpha hyperparameter.
        b (float): Beta hyperparameter.
    """

    a: float  # alpha hyperparameter
    b: float  # beta hyperparameter

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x):
        """Apply the custom activation function.

        Args:
            x: Input tensor.

        Returns:
            Tensor: Transformed input tensor.
        """
        return multiply(
            add(self.b, multiply(sigmoid(multiply(self.a, x)), subtract(1.0, self.b))),
            x,
        )

docs.title: CustomActivation
docs.text:
Bases: Layer

TensorFlow custom activation function matching arXiv:2106.03846.

This is kept for compatibility when loading TensorFlow models. The JAX version (CustomActivation_jax) should be used for new JAX models.

Source code in src/UPanda/integrated_model_jax.py 
class CustomActivation(Layer):
    """TensorFlow custom activation function matching arXiv:2106.03846.

    This is kept for compatibility when loading TensorFlow models.
    The JAX version (CustomActivation_jax) should be used for new JAX models.
    """

    def build(self, input_shape):
        # Trainable weight variables for alpha and beta initialized with random normal distribution
        self.alpha = self.add_weight(
            name="alpha",
            shape=input_shape[1:],
            initializer="random_normal",
            trainable=True,
        )
        self.beta = self.add_weight(
            name="beta",
            shape=input_shape[1:],
            initializer="random_normal",
            trainable=True,
        )
        super(CustomActivation, self).build(input_shape)

    def call(self, inputs):
        return (self.beta + tf.sigmoid(self.alpha * inputs) * (1 - self.beta)) * inputs

class CustomLoss(Layer):
    def __init__(self, element_weights=None, **kwargs):
        super(CustomLoss, self).__init__(**kwargs)
        self.element_weights = (
            tf.convert_to_tensor(element_weights, dtype=tf.float32)
            if element_weights is not None
            else tf.constant(1.0, dtype=tf.float32)
        )

    def call(self, y_true, y_pred):
        # Compute element-wise squared errors
        squared_errors = tf.square(y_true - y_pred)

        if self.element_weights is not None:
            # Apply element-wise weights
            squared_errors = squared_errors / self.element_weights

        # Compute the mean of squared errors
        return tf.reduce_mean(squared_errors)

    def get_config(self):
        config = super(CustomLoss, self).get_config()
        config.update({"element_weights": self.element_weights.numpy()})
        return config

class IntegratedModel:
    """JAX-compatible wrapper for TensorFlow-trained IntegratedModel.

    This class mirrors integrated_model.IntegratedModel but uses JAX for predictions,
    enabling JIT compilation and automatic differentiation.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        keras_model,
        input_scaler,
        output_scaler,
        parameter_names,
        temp_file=None,
        offset=None,
        log_preprocess=False,
        cheby_preprocess=False,
        cheby_meta=None,
        rescaling_factor=None,
        pca=None,
        pca_scaler=None,
        rescale_by_as=False,
        galaxy_bias_config=None,
        verbose=False,
    ):
        self.model = keras_model
        self.input_scaler = input_scaler
        self.output_scaler = output_scaler
        self.offset = offset
        self.rescaling_factor = rescaling_factor
        self.temp_file = temp_file
        self.train_losses = []
        self.val_losses = []
        self.log_preprocess = log_preprocess
        self.cheby_preprocess = cheby_preprocess
        self.cheby_meta = cheby_meta
        self.parameter_names = parameter_names
        self.pca = pca
        self.pca_scaler = pca_scaler
        self.rescale_by_as = rescale_by_as

        # Galaxy bias rescaling configuration (metadata-driven)
        # Format: {
        #   'enabled': bool,
        #   'linear': [(start_idx, end_idx, bias_param_name), ...],  # cross-spectra scale as b_i
        #   'quadratic': [(start_idx, end_idx, bias_param_name), ...],  # auto-spectra scale as b_i^2
        # }
        # Set to None to disable, or provide dict with 'enabled': True and index ranges
        self.galaxy_bias_config = galaxy_bias_config
        self.verbose = verbose

    def predict(self, data_dict):
        if self.parameter_names is not None:
            required_keys = set(sorted(data_dict.keys()))
            expected_keys = set(self.parameter_names)
            if not expected_keys.issubset(required_keys):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Input dictionary keys {required_keys} do not match expected keys {expected_keys}"
                )

        # Map parameter values to the correct positions in the input matrix
        data = stack([asarray(data_dict[key]) for key in self.parameter_names], axis=1)

            # print(data)
            # print(self.parameter_names)
            # print(self.scaler_mean_in)

        # Ensure scaler arrays have the right shape for broadcasting
        scaler_mean_in = self.scaler_mean_in.reshape(1, -1)
        scaler_scale_in = self.scaler_scale_in.reshape(1, -1)
        scaled_data = (data - scaler_mean_in) / scaler_scale_in

        # Store A_s values if we need to rescale (matches integrated_model.py)
        amplitudes = None
        if self.rescale_by_as and "ln10^{10}A_s" in self.parameter_names:
            # Find the index of the A_s parameter
            as_index = list(self.parameter_names).index("ln10^{10}A_s")
            ln_10_10_as = data[:, as_index]
            amplitudes = exp(ln_10_10_as) * 1e-10

        # Convert to TensorFlow tensor
        scaled_data = array(scaled_data, dtype=float32)
        prediction = self.jax_model.apply(self.jax_params, scaled_data)

        # Inverse transforms applied in reverse order of training (matches integrated_model.py)

        # Apply inverse PCA transform if PCA is used
        if self.pca is not None:
            scaler_scale_out = self.scaler_scale_out.reshape(1, -1)
            scaler_mean_out = self.scaler_mean_out.reshape(1, -1)
            prediction = prediction * scaler_scale_out + scaler_mean_out

            # Invert the PCA using the mean and components
            prediction = dot(prediction, self.pca_components) + self.pca_mean
            prediction = prediction * self.pca_scaler_scale + self.pca_scaler_mean
        elif self.cheby_preprocess and self.cheby_meta is not None:
            # Inverse Chebyshev transform
            scaler_scale_out = self.scaler_scale_out.reshape(1, -1)
            scaler_mean_out = self.scaler_mean_out.reshape(1, -1)
            prediction = prediction * scaler_scale_out + scaler_mean_out

            # Undo min-max scaling
            coeffs = prediction * self.cheby_meta['c_denom'] + self.cheby_meta['c_min']

            # Reconstruct: coeffs -> standardized D_ell -> D_ell -> C_ell
            y_std = dot(coeffs, self.cheby_meta['V'].T)
            y_D = y_std * self.cheby_meta['D_std'] + self.cheby_meta['D_mean']
            prediction = y_D / self.cheby_meta['ell_factor']
        else:
            scaler_scale_out = self.scaler_scale_out.reshape(1, -1)
            scaler_mean_out = self.scaler_mean_out.reshape(1, -1)
            prediction = prediction * scaler_scale_out + scaler_mean_out

        # Inverse offset and log
        if self.log_preprocess:
            prediction = exp(prediction) + 2 * self.offset

        # Rescale by A_s if needed
        if self.rescale_by_as and amplitudes is not None:
            prediction = prediction * amplitudes[:, newaxis]

        # Apply galaxy bias rescaling if configured
        prediction = self._apply_galaxy_bias_rescaling(prediction, data_dict)

        return prediction

    def _apply_galaxy_bias_rescaling(self, prediction, data_dict):
        """Apply galaxy bias rescaling to prediction based on configuration.

        Compatible with JAX vmap and jit.

        Auto-spectra (dd_ii, gg_ii) scale as b_i^2 (quadratic).
        Cross-spectra (kad_i, td_i, kg_i, tg_i) scale as b_i (linear).

        Args:
            prediction: JAX array of shape (n_samples, n_output).
            data_dict: Dictionary with bias parameter values.

        Returns:
            Rescaled prediction array.
        """
        if self.galaxy_bias_config is None:
            return prediction
        if not self.galaxy_bias_config.get('enabled', False):
            return prediction

        # Quadratic rescaling for auto-spectra
        for start_idx, end_idx, bias_name in self.galaxy_bias_config.get('quadratic', []):
            if bias_name in data_dict:
                bias_vals = data_dict[bias_name]
                if not hasattr(bias_vals, 'at'):
                    bias_vals = array(bias_vals)
                prediction = prediction.at[:, start_idx:end_idx].multiply(
                    (bias_vals ** 2)[:, newaxis]
                )

        # Linear rescaling for cross-spectra
        for start_idx, end_idx, bias_name in self.galaxy_bias_config.get('linear', []):
            if bias_name in data_dict:
                bias_vals = data_dict[bias_name]
                if not hasattr(bias_vals, 'at'):
                    bias_vals = array(bias_vals)
                prediction = prediction.at[:, start_idx:end_idx].multiply(
                    bias_vals[:, newaxis]
                )

        return prediction

    def save(self, filename):
        """Save IntegratedModel to disk.

        Saves the model in a format compatible with integrated_model.IntegratedModel.
        Note: This saves the original TensorFlow model, not the JAX conversion.

        Args:
            filename (str): Base filename (without suffix) where model will
                be saved. Files will be saved as:
                - {filename}_model.h5 (Keras model)
                - {filename}.pkl (other attributes)
        """
        # Save the Keras model in the .h5 format
        self.model.save(filename + "_model.h5")

        # attributes list must match integrated_model.py exactly (12 attributes)
        attributes = [
            self.input_scaler,
            self.output_scaler,
            self.offset,
            self.log_preprocess,
            self.pca,
            self.pca_scaler,
            self.parameter_names,
            self.rescaling_factor,
            self.rescale_by_as,
            self.cheby_preprocess,
            self.cheby_meta,
            self.galaxy_bias_config,
        ]

        with open(filename + ".pkl", "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(attributes, f)

        logger.debug("Model saved to %s_model.h5", filename)

    def restore(self, filename):
        """Load pre-saved IntegratedModel from disk.

        Transform tf weights to jax weights dynamically and initialize the jax model

        Parameters:
            filename (str): filename tag (without suffix) where model was saved
        """
        # Load the Keras model from the .h5 format
        tf_model = load_model(
            filename + "_model.h5",
            custom_objects={
                "CustomActivation": CustomActivation,
                "CustomLoss": CustomLoss,
            },
            compile=False,
        )

        self.model = tf_model
        tf_params = []
        for layer in tf_model.layers:
            weights = layer.get_weights()
            if weights:  # Check if the layer has parameters
                tf_params.append(weights)

        # load in the weights and hyperparameters
        tf_weights = []
        tf_hyperparams = []
        for i, layer in enumerate(tf_params):
            if i % 2 == 0:
                tf_weights.append(tf_params[i])
            else:
                tf_hyperparams.append(tf_params[i])

        # Load the remaining attributes
        with open(filename + ".pkl", "rb") as f:
            attributes = pickle.load(f)

            from UPanda._model_io import decode_attributes
            for key, value in decode_attributes(attributes).items():
                setattr(self, key, value)

        self.scaler_mean_in = self.input_scaler.mean_
        self.scaler_scale_in = self.input_scaler.scale_

        logger.debug("input scaler mean shape: %s", self.scaler_mean_in.shape)

        self.scaler_scale_out = self.output_scaler.scale_
        self.scaler_mean_out = self.output_scaler.mean_

        logger.debug("output scaler mean shape: %s", self.scaler_mean_out.shape)

        try:
            self.pca_scaler_mean = self.pca_scaler.mean_
            self.pca_scaler_scale = self.pca_scaler.scale_
        except AttributeError:
            logger.debug("No PCA scaler found in model")

        try:
            self.pca_mean = self.pca.mean_
            self.pca_components = self.pca.components_
        except AttributeError:
            logger.debug("No PCA found in model")

        self.jax_model = MyNetwork(hyper_params=tf_hyperparams, weights=tf_weights)

        # Initialize the model with dummy data
        input_shape = tf_weights[0][0].shape[0]  # the input shape of the first layer
        rng = random.PRNGKey(0)
        dummy_input = ones((1, input_shape))
        params = self.jax_model.init(rng, dummy_input)

        # Flatten the parameters dictionary
        flattened_params = traverse_util.flatten_dict(params)

        # Replace the initialized parameters with your pre-trained weights and hyperparameters
        for i, layer_path in enumerate(flattened_params.keys()):
            if (
                "CustomActivation" in layer_path
            ):  # Assuming this is the name of your custom activation layers
                # Replace hyperparameters
                flattened_params[layer_path] = tf_hyperparams[i]
            else:
                # Replace weights and biases
                flattened_params[layer_path] = tf_weights[i]

        # Unflatten the parameters dictionary
        self.jax_params = traverse_util.unflatten_dict(flattened_params)

        logger.debug("IntegratedModel (JAX) restore successful")

def insert_zero_columns(prediction, zero_columns_indices):
    """Insert zero columns at specified indices in predictions.

    This function is useful for inserting masked or invalid multipole bins
    back into power spectrum predictions, maintaining compatibility with
    data vectors that include these bins.

    Args:
        prediction (ndarray): Prediction array with shape (n_samples, n_features).
        zero_columns_indices (array-like): Indices where zero columns should
            be inserted.

    Returns:
        ndarray: Prediction array with zero columns inserted. Shape is
            (n_samples, n_features + len(zero_columns_indices)).
    """
    # Ensure prediction is a JAX array if JAX is enabled
    if is_jax:
        import jax.numpy as jnp

        if not hasattr(prediction, "at"):
            prediction = jnp.array(prediction)

    # Total number of columns in the final output
    num_columns = prediction.shape[1] + len(zero_columns_indices)

    # Initialize the final_prediction array
    final_prediction = zeros((prediction.shape[0], num_columns))

    # Ensure final_prediction is a JAX array if JAX is enabled
    if is_jax:
        import jax.numpy as jnp

        if not hasattr(final_prediction, "at"):
            final_prediction = jnp.array(final_prediction)

    # Indices in final_prediction where values from prediction will be inserted
    non_zero_indices = delete(arange(num_columns), zero_columns_indices)

    # Ensure non_zero_indices is a JAX array if JAX is enabled
    if is_jax:
        import jax.numpy as jnp

        if not hasattr(non_zero_indices, "at"):
            non_zero_indices = jnp.array(non_zero_indices)

    # Insert values from prediction into the correct positions in final_prediction
    # Use .at syntax for JAX arrays, or regular indexing for NumPy
    if is_jax and hasattr(final_prediction, "at"):
        final_prediction = final_prediction.at[:, non_zero_indices].set(prediction)
    else:
        # Fallback for NumPy arrays
        final_prediction[:, non_zero_indices] = prediction

    return final_prediction

TensorFlow/Keras-based integrated emulator models for cosmological predictions.

This module provides the IntegratedModel class which wraps TensorFlow/Keras neural network models for fast cosmological predictions. It handles input/output scaling, PCA compression, log preprocessing, Chebyshev preprocessing, and A_s rescaling.

The module includes custom activation functions and loss functions designed for cosmological emulation tasks.

class CustomActivation(Layer):
    """Custom activation function matching arXiv:2106.03846.

    This activation function uses trainable parameters alpha and beta to
    create a learnable activation: (β + sigmoid(αx) * (1 - β)) * x

    This is designed for cosmological emulation tasks where the activation
    shape can significantly impact model performance.
    """

    def build(self, input_shape):
        """Build the layer by creating trainable weights.

        Args:
            input_shape: Shape of the input tensor.
        """
        # Trainable weight variables for alpha and beta initialized with random normal distribution
        self.alpha = self.add_weight(
            name="alpha",
            shape=input_shape[1:],
            initializer="random_normal",
            trainable=True,
        )
        self.beta = self.add_weight(
            name="beta",
            shape=input_shape[1:],
            initializer="random_normal",
            trainable=True,
        )
        super(CustomActivation, self).build(input_shape)

    def call(self, inputs):
        """Apply the custom activation function.

        Args:
            inputs: Input tensor.

        Returns:
            Tensor: Transformed input tensor.
        """
        return (self.beta + tf.sigmoid(self.alpha * inputs) * (1 - self.beta)) * inputs

class CustomLoss(Layer):
    """Custom loss function with element-wise weighting.

    This loss function allows for element-wise weighting of the squared error,
    which is useful when different parts of the output spectrum have different
    importance or uncertainty.

    Attributes:
        element_weights (Tensor): Weights for each element of the output.
    """

    def __init__(self, element_weights=None, **kwargs):
        """Initialize the custom loss function.

        Args:
            element_weights (array-like, optional): Weights for each output
                element. If None, all elements are weighted equally.
                Defaults to None.
            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments passed to parent class.
        """
        super(CustomLoss, self).__init__(**kwargs)
        self.element_weights = (
            tf.convert_to_tensor(element_weights, dtype=tf.float32)
            if element_weights is not None
            else tf.constant(1.0, dtype=tf.float32)
        )

    def call(self, y_true, y_pred):
        """Compute the weighted mean squared error.

        Args:
            y_true: True values.
            y_pred: Predicted values.

        Returns:
            Tensor: Scalar loss value.
        """
        # Compute element-wise squared errors
        squared_errors = tf.square(y_true - y_pred)

        if self.element_weights is not None:
            # Apply element-wise weights
            squared_errors = squared_errors / self.element_weights

        # Compute the mean of squared errors
        return tf.reduce_mean(squared_errors)

    def get_config(self):
        """Get configuration dictionary for serialization.

        Returns:
            dict: Configuration dictionary.
        """
        config = super(CustomLoss, self).get_config()
        config.update({"element_weights": self.element_weights.numpy()})
        return config

class IntegratedModel:
    """Integrated emulator model wrapper for TensorFlow/Keras neural networks.

    This class wraps a trained Keras model with preprocessing/postprocessing
    steps including input/output scaling, PCA compression, log preprocessing,
    Chebyshev preprocessing, and A_s rescaling.
    It provides a unified interface for making cosmological predictions from
    parameter dictionaries.

    Attributes:
        model (Model): Trained Keras model.
        input_scaler (StandardScaler): Scaler for input parameters.
        output_scaler (StandardScaler): Scaler for output predictions.
        parameter_names (list): List of parameter names in order.
        pca (PCA, optional): PCA transformer for output compression.
        pca_scaler (StandardScaler, optional): Scaler for PCA space.
        log_preprocess (bool): Whether to apply log preprocessing.
        cheby_preprocess (bool): Whether to apply Chebyshev preprocessing.
        cheby_meta (dict, optional): Chebyshev metadata for inverse transform.
        rescale_by_as (bool): Whether to rescale by A_s.
        offset (float, optional): Offset for log preprocessing.
        rescaling_factor (float, optional): Rescaling factor.
        temp_file (str, optional): Temporary file path.
        train_losses (list): Training loss history.
        val_losses (list): Validation loss history.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        keras_model,
        input_scaler,
        output_scaler,
        parameter_names,
        temp_file=None,
        offset=None,
        log_preprocess=False,
        cheby_preprocess=False,
        cheby_meta=None,
        rescaling_factor=None,
        pca=None,
        pca_scaler=None,
        rescale_by_as=False,
        galaxy_bias_config=None,
    ):
        """Initialize the integrated model.

        Args:
            keras_model (Model): Trained Keras model.
            input_scaler (StandardScaler): Scaler fitted on input parameters.
            output_scaler (StandardScaler): Scaler fitted on output predictions.
            parameter_names (list): List of parameter names in the order
                expected by the model.
            temp_file (str, optional): Path to temporary file. Defaults to None.
            offset (float, optional): Offset for log preprocessing. Defaults to None.
            log_preprocess (bool, optional): Whether to apply log preprocessing
                to inputs. Defaults to False.
            cheby_preprocess (bool, optional): Whether to apply Chebyshev
                preprocessing for oscillatory signals like TE spectra. Defaults to False.
            cheby_meta (dict, optional): Chebyshev metadata containing ell_factor,
                D_mean, D_std, V, c_min, c_denom for inverse transform. Required if
                cheby_preprocess is True. Defaults to None.
            rescaling_factor (float, optional): Rescaling factor for outputs.
                Defaults to None.
            pca (PCA, optional): PCA transformer for output compression.
                Defaults to None.
            pca_scaler (StandardScaler, optional): Scaler for PCA-transformed
                outputs. Defaults to None.
            rescale_by_as (bool, optional): Whether to rescale outputs by
                A_s parameter. Defaults to False.
        """
        self.model = keras_model
        self.input_scaler = input_scaler
        self.output_scaler = output_scaler
        self.offset = offset
        self.rescaling_factor = rescaling_factor
        self.temp_file = temp_file
        self.train_losses = []
        self.val_losses = []
        self.log_preprocess = log_preprocess
        self.cheby_preprocess = cheby_preprocess
        self.cheby_meta = cheby_meta
        self.parameter_names = parameter_names
        self.pca = pca
        self.pca_scaler = pca_scaler
        self.rescale_by_as = rescale_by_as

        # Galaxy bias rescaling configuration (metadata-driven)
        # Format: {
        #   'enabled': bool,
        #   'linear': [(start_idx, end_idx, bias_param_name), ...],  # cross-spectra scale as b_i
        #   'quadratic': [(start_idx, end_idx, bias_param_name), ...],  # auto-spectra scale as b_i^2
        # }
        # Set to None to disable, or provide dict with 'enabled': True and index ranges
        self.galaxy_bias_config = galaxy_bias_config

    def predict(self, data_dict):
        """Make predictions from cosmological parameters.

        Args:
            data_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping parameter names to arrays
                of parameter values. All arrays must have the same length
                (number of samples).

        Returns:
            ndarray: Predicted outputs. Shape is (n_samples, n_output_features).

        Raises:
            ValueError: If required parameter keys are missing from data_dict.
        """
        if self.parameter_names is not None:
            required_keys = set(sorted(data_dict.keys()))
            expected_keys = set(self.parameter_names)
            if not expected_keys.issubset(required_keys):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Input dictionary keys {required_keys} do not match expected keys {expected_keys}"
                )

        # Map parameter values to the correct positions in the input matrix
        num_samples = len(
            next(iter(data_dict.values()))
        )  # Assuming all values in data_dict have the same length
        num_features = len(self.parameter_names)
        data = np.empty((num_samples, num_features))
        for i, key in enumerate(self.parameter_names):
            data[:, i] = data_dict[key]

        # Store A_s values if we need to rescale
        amplitudes = None
        if self.rescale_by_as and "ln10^{10}A_s" in self.parameter_names:
            # Find the index of the A_s parameter
            as_index = list(self.parameter_names).index("ln10^{10}A_s")
            ln_10_10_as = data[:, as_index]
            amplitudes = exp(ln_10_10_as) * 1e-10

        scaled_data = (data - self.scaler_mean_in) / self.scaler_scale_in
        prediction = self.model(tf.convert_to_tensor(scaled_data, dtype=tf.float32))

        # Inverse transforms applied in reverse order of training

        # Apply inverse PCA transform if PCA is used
        if self.pca is not None:
            prediction = prediction * self.scaler_scale_out + self.scaler_mean_out
            prediction = self.pca.inverse_transform(prediction)
            prediction = self.pca_scaler.inverse_transform(prediction)
        elif self.cheby_preprocess and self.cheby_meta is not None:
            # Inverse Chebyshev transform
            # 1. Unscale from output scaler
            prediction = prediction * self.scaler_scale_out + self.scaler_mean_out

            # 2. Undo min-max scaling
            coeffs = prediction * self.cheby_meta['c_denom'] + self.cheby_meta['c_min']

            # 3. Reconstruct: coeffs -> standardized D_ell -> D_ell -> C_ell
            y_std = coeffs @ self.cheby_meta['V'].T
            y_D = y_std * self.cheby_meta['D_std'] + self.cheby_meta['D_mean']
            prediction = y_D / self.cheby_meta['ell_factor']
        else:
            prediction = prediction * self.scaler_scale_out + self.scaler_mean_out

        # Inverse offset and log
        if self.log_preprocess:
            prediction = np.exp(prediction) + 2 * self.offset

        # Rescale by A_s if needed
        if self.rescale_by_as and amplitudes is not None:
            prediction = prediction * amplitudes[:, newaxis]

        # Apply galaxy bias rescaling if configured
        prediction = self._apply_galaxy_bias_rescaling(prediction, data_dict)

        return prediction

    def _apply_galaxy_bias_rescaling(self, prediction, data_dict):
        """Apply galaxy bias rescaling to prediction based on configuration.

        Auto-spectra (dd_ii, gg_ii) scale as b_i^2 (quadratic).
        Cross-spectra (kad_i, td_i, kg_i, tg_i) scale as b_i (linear).

        Args:
            prediction: Array of shape (n_samples, n_output).
            data_dict: Dictionary with bias parameter values.

        Returns:
            Rescaled prediction array.
        """
        if self.galaxy_bias_config is None:
            return prediction
        if not self.galaxy_bias_config.get('enabled', False):
            return prediction

        # TensorFlow tensors are immutable. Preserve the input type and avoid
        # modifying arrays supplied by callers as well.
        concatenate = tf.concat if tf.is_tensor(prediction) else np.concatenate
        for kind, exponent in [('quadratic', 2), ('linear', 1)]:
            for start, end, name in self.galaxy_bias_config.get(kind, []):
                if name in data_dict:
                    bias = np.asarray(data_dict[name]) ** exponent
                    prediction = concatenate([
                        prediction[:, :start],
                        prediction[:, start:end] * bias[:, None],
                        prediction[:, end:],
                    ], axis=1)

        return prediction

    def compute_gradient(self, data_dict):
        """Compute gradient of predictions with respect to input parameters.

        Args:
            data_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping parameter names to arrays
                of parameter values.

        Returns:
            ndarray: Gradient of outputs with respect to inputs. Shape is
                (n_samples, n_output_features, n_input_features).

        Raises:
            ValueError: If parameter keys don't match expected keys exactly.
        """
        if self.parameter_names is not None:
            required_keys = set(sorted(data_dict.keys()))
            expected_keys = set(self.parameter_names)
            if required_keys != expected_keys:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Input dictionary keys {required_keys} do not match expected keys {expected_keys}"
                )

        # Differentiate with respect to raw input parameters. NumPy/sklearn
        # inverse transforms inside GradientTape disconnect the graph.
        data = tf.convert_to_tensor(
            np.column_stack([data_dict[key] for key in self.parameter_names]),
            dtype=tf.float32,
        )
        def constant(value):
            return tf.convert_to_tensor(value, dtype=data.dtype)

        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            tape.watch(data)
            scaled = (data - constant(self.input_scaler.mean_)) / constant(self.input_scaler.scale_)
            prediction = self.model(scaled, training=False)
            prediction = prediction * constant(self.output_scaler.scale_) + constant(self.output_scaler.mean_)
            if self.pca is not None:
                prediction = tf.linalg.matmul(prediction, constant(self.pca.components_)) + constant(self.pca.mean_)
                prediction = prediction * constant(self.pca_scaler.scale_) + constant(self.pca_scaler.mean_)
            elif self.cheby_preprocess and self.cheby_meta is not None:
                meta = self.cheby_meta
                coefficients = prediction * constant(meta['c_denom']) + constant(meta['c_min'])
                prediction = tf.linalg.matmul(coefficients, constant(meta['V']), transpose_b=True)
                prediction = (prediction * constant(meta['D_std']) + constant(meta['D_mean'])) / constant(meta['ell_factor'])
            if self.log_preprocess:
                prediction = tf.exp(prediction) + 2 * self.offset
            if self.rescale_by_as and "ln10^{10}A_s" in self.parameter_names:
                index = list(self.parameter_names).index("ln10^{10}A_s")
                prediction = prediction * (tf.exp(data[:, index]) * 1e-10)[:, None]
            if self.galaxy_bias_config and self.galaxy_bias_config.get('enabled', False):
                for kind, exponent in [('quadratic', 2), ('linear', 1)]:
                    for start, end, name in self.galaxy_bias_config.get(kind, []):
                        if name in self.parameter_names:
                            bias = data[:, list(self.parameter_names).index(name)] ** exponent
                            prediction = tf.concat([
                                prediction[:, :start],
                                prediction[:, start:end] * bias[:, None],
                                prediction[:, end:],
                            ], axis=1)
        return tape.batch_jacobian(prediction, data).numpy()

    def train(self, X, y, learning_rates=[1e-3, 5e-4, 1e-4, 5e-5], *args, **kwargs):
        """Train the model with learning rate scheduling.

        Args:
            X (ndarray): Training input data. Shape (n_samples, n_features).
            y (ndarray): Training target data. Shape (n_samples, n_outputs).
            learning_rates (list, optional): List of learning rates to use
                sequentially. Defaults to [1e-3, 5e-4, 1e-4, 5e-5].
            *args: Additional positional arguments passed to model.fit().
            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments passed to model.fit(),
                including 'epochs', 'validation_split', 'batch_size', etc.
        """
        # Scale the training data
        X_scaled = self.input_scaler.transform(X)
        y_scaled = self.output_scaler.transform(y)

        early_stopping = EarlyStopping(
            monitor="val_loss", patience=100, verbose=1, restore_best_weights=True
        )

        for lr in learning_rates:
            print(f"\nTraining with learning rate: {lr}")

            # Compile the model with the current learning rate
            custom_loss = CustomLoss(element_weights=self.rescaling_factor)
            self.model.compile(
                optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lr), loss=custom_loss
            )

            # Get the total number of epochs (this can be adjusted based on your needs)
            total_epochs = kwargs.get("epochs", 200)

            # Wrap the training in a tqdm progress bar
            with tqdm(total=total_epochs, unit="epoch", postfix={}) as pbar:
                # Custom callback to update tqdm progress bar after each epoch and display validation loss (in scientific notation)
                def on_epoch_end(epoch, logs):
                    train_loss = logs.get(
                        "loss", 0.0
                    )  # Get the training loss from logs
                    val_loss = logs.get(
                        "val_loss", 0.0
                    )  # Get the validation loss from logs
                    pbar.set_postfix(
                        {
                            "train_loss": f"{train_loss:.2e}",
                            "val_loss": f"{val_loss:.2e}",
                        }
                    )  # Show losses in scientific notation
                    self.train_losses.append(train_loss)
                    self.val_losses.append(val_loss)
                    pbar.update(1)

                # Train the model with early stopping and tqdm callback
                self.model.fit(
                    X_scaled,
                    y_scaled,
                    callbacks=[
                        early_stopping,
                        LambdaCallback(on_epoch_end=on_epoch_end),
                    ],
                    verbose=0,  # Turn off default verbose
                    *args,
                    **kwargs,
                )

            # Optionally save the model at the end of the training cycle
            if self.temp_file is not None:
                self.save(self.temp_file)

    def save(self, filename):
        """Save IntegratedModel to disk.

        Saves the Keras model as an HDF5 file and other attributes (scalers,
        PCA, etc.) as a pickle file.

        Args:
            filename (str): Base filename (without suffix) where model will
                be saved. Files will be saved as:
                - {filename}_model.h5 (Keras model)
                - {filename}.pkl (other attributes)
        """
        # Save the Keras model in the .h5 format to handle custom objects like CustomActivation
        self.model.save(filename + "_model.h5")

        # attributes, excluding the model which we've saved separately
        attributes = [
            self.input_scaler,
            self.output_scaler,
            self.offset,
            self.log_preprocess,
            self.pca,
            self.pca_scaler,
            self.parameter_names,
            self.rescaling_factor,
            self.rescale_by_as,
            self.cheby_preprocess,
            self.cheby_meta,
            self.galaxy_bias_config,
        ]

        # Save the remaining attributes to file
        with open(filename + ".pkl", "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(attributes, f)

        print(f"Model saved to {filename}_model.h5")

    def restore(self, filename):
        """Load IntegratedModel from disk.

        Loads the Keras model from HDF5 file and other attributes from
        pickle file. Supports backward compatibility with older model formats.

        Args:
            filename (str): Base filename (without suffix) where model was
                saved. Files should be:
                - {filename}_model.h5 (Keras model)
                - {filename}.pkl (other attributes)
        """
        # Load the Keras model from the .h5 format
        self.model = load_model(
            filename + "_model.h5",
            custom_objects={
                "CustomActivation": CustomActivation,
                "CustomLoss": CustomLoss,
            },
            compile=False,
        )

        # Load the remaining attributes
        with open(filename + ".pkl", "rb") as f:
            attributes = pickle.load(f)

            from UPanda._model_io import decode_attributes
            for key, value in decode_attributes(attributes).items():
                setattr(self, key, value)

        self.scaler_mean_in = self.input_scaler.mean_  # Mean of the features
        self.scaler_scale_in = (
            self.input_scaler.scale_
        )  # Standard deviation of the features

        self.scaler_scale_out = (
            self.output_scaler.scale_
        )  # Standard deviation of the features
        self.scaler_mean_out = (
            self.output_scaler.mean_
        )  # Standard deviation of the features

        print("restore successful")

def __init__(
    self,
    keras_model,
    input_scaler,
    output_scaler,
    parameter_names,
    temp_file=None,
    offset=None,
    log_preprocess=False,
    cheby_preprocess=False,
    cheby_meta=None,
    rescaling_factor=None,
    pca=None,
    pca_scaler=None,
    rescale_by_as=False,
    galaxy_bias_config=None,
):
    """Initialize the integrated model.

    Args:
        keras_model (Model): Trained Keras model.
        input_scaler (StandardScaler): Scaler fitted on input parameters.
        output_scaler (StandardScaler): Scaler fitted on output predictions.
        parameter_names (list): List of parameter names in the order
            expected by the model.
        temp_file (str, optional): Path to temporary file. Defaults to None.
        offset (float, optional): Offset for log preprocessing. Defaults to None.
        log_preprocess (bool, optional): Whether to apply log preprocessing
            to inputs. Defaults to False.
        cheby_preprocess (bool, optional): Whether to apply Chebyshev
            preprocessing for oscillatory signals like TE spectra. Defaults to False.
        cheby_meta (dict, optional): Chebyshev metadata containing ell_factor,
            D_mean, D_std, V, c_min, c_denom for inverse transform. Required if
            cheby_preprocess is True. Defaults to None.
        rescaling_factor (float, optional): Rescaling factor for outputs.
            Defaults to None.
        pca (PCA, optional): PCA transformer for output compression.
            Defaults to None.
        pca_scaler (StandardScaler, optional): Scaler for PCA-transformed
            outputs. Defaults to None.
        rescale_by_as (bool, optional): Whether to rescale outputs by
            A_s parameter. Defaults to False.
    """
    self.model = keras_model
    self.input_scaler = input_scaler
    self.output_scaler = output_scaler
    self.offset = offset
    self.rescaling_factor = rescaling_factor
    self.temp_file = temp_file
    self.train_losses = []
    self.val_losses = []
    self.log_preprocess = log_preprocess
    self.cheby_preprocess = cheby_preprocess
    self.cheby_meta = cheby_meta
    self.parameter_names = parameter_names
    self.pca = pca
    self.pca_scaler = pca_scaler
    self.rescale_by_as = rescale_by_as

    # Galaxy bias rescaling configuration (metadata-driven)
    # Format: {
    #   'enabled': bool,
    #   'linear': [(start_idx, end_idx, bias_param_name), ...],  # cross-spectra scale as b_i
    #   'quadratic': [(start_idx, end_idx, bias_param_name), ...],  # auto-spectra scale as b_i^2
    # }
    # Set to None to disable, or provide dict with 'enabled': True and index ranges
    self.galaxy_bias_config = galaxy_bias_config

def predict(self, data_dict):
    """Make predictions from cosmological parameters.

    Args:
        data_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping parameter names to arrays
            of parameter values. All arrays must have the same length
            (number of samples).

    Returns:
        ndarray: Predicted outputs. Shape is (n_samples, n_output_features).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If required parameter keys are missing from data_dict.
    """
    if self.parameter_names is not None:
        required_keys = set(sorted(data_dict.keys()))
        expected_keys = set(self.parameter_names)
        if not expected_keys.issubset(required_keys):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Input dictionary keys {required_keys} do not match expected keys {expected_keys}"
            )

    # Map parameter values to the correct positions in the input matrix
    num_samples = len(
        next(iter(data_dict.values()))
    )  # Assuming all values in data_dict have the same length
    num_features = len(self.parameter_names)
    data = np.empty((num_samples, num_features))
    for i, key in enumerate(self.parameter_names):
        data[:, i] = data_dict[key]

    # Store A_s values if we need to rescale
    amplitudes = None
    if self.rescale_by_as and "ln10^{10}A_s" in self.parameter_names:
        # Find the index of the A_s parameter
        as_index = list(self.parameter_names).index("ln10^{10}A_s")
        ln_10_10_as = data[:, as_index]
        amplitudes = exp(ln_10_10_as) * 1e-10

    scaled_data = (data - self.scaler_mean_in) / self.scaler_scale_in
    prediction = self.model(tf.convert_to_tensor(scaled_data, dtype=tf.float32))

    # Inverse transforms applied in reverse order of training

    # Apply inverse PCA transform if PCA is used
    if self.pca is not None:
        prediction = prediction * self.scaler_scale_out + self.scaler_mean_out
        prediction = self.pca.inverse_transform(prediction)
        prediction = self.pca_scaler.inverse_transform(prediction)
    elif self.cheby_preprocess and self.cheby_meta is not None:
        # Inverse Chebyshev transform
        # 1. Unscale from output scaler
        prediction = prediction * self.scaler_scale_out + self.scaler_mean_out

        # 2. Undo min-max scaling
        coeffs = prediction * self.cheby_meta['c_denom'] + self.cheby_meta['c_min']

        # 3. Reconstruct: coeffs -> standardized D_ell -> D_ell -> C_ell
        y_std = coeffs @ self.cheby_meta['V'].T
        y_D = y_std * self.cheby_meta['D_std'] + self.cheby_meta['D_mean']
        prediction = y_D / self.cheby_meta['ell_factor']
    else:
        prediction = prediction * self.scaler_scale_out + self.scaler_mean_out

    # Inverse offset and log
    if self.log_preprocess:
        prediction = np.exp(prediction) + 2 * self.offset

    # Rescale by A_s if needed
    if self.rescale_by_as and amplitudes is not None:
        prediction = prediction * amplitudes[:, newaxis]

    # Apply galaxy bias rescaling if configured
    prediction = self._apply_galaxy_bias_rescaling(prediction, data_dict)

    return prediction

def compute_gradient(self, data_dict):
    """Compute gradient of predictions with respect to input parameters.

    Args:
        data_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping parameter names to arrays
            of parameter values.

    Returns:
        ndarray: Gradient of outputs with respect to inputs. Shape is
            (n_samples, n_output_features, n_input_features).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If parameter keys don't match expected keys exactly.
    """
    if self.parameter_names is not None:
        required_keys = set(sorted(data_dict.keys()))
        expected_keys = set(self.parameter_names)
        if required_keys != expected_keys:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Input dictionary keys {required_keys} do not match expected keys {expected_keys}"
            )

    # Differentiate with respect to raw input parameters. NumPy/sklearn
    # inverse transforms inside GradientTape disconnect the graph.
    data = tf.convert_to_tensor(
        np.column_stack([data_dict[key] for key in self.parameter_names]),
        dtype=tf.float32,
    )
    def constant(value):
        return tf.convert_to_tensor(value, dtype=data.dtype)

    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        tape.watch(data)
        scaled = (data - constant(self.input_scaler.mean_)) / constant(self.input_scaler.scale_)
        prediction = self.model(scaled, training=False)
        prediction = prediction * constant(self.output_scaler.scale_) + constant(self.output_scaler.mean_)
        if self.pca is not None:
            prediction = tf.linalg.matmul(prediction, constant(self.pca.components_)) + constant(self.pca.mean_)
            prediction = prediction * constant(self.pca_scaler.scale_) + constant(self.pca_scaler.mean_)
        elif self.cheby_preprocess and self.cheby_meta is not None:
            meta = self.cheby_meta
            coefficients = prediction * constant(meta['c_denom']) + constant(meta['c_min'])
            prediction = tf.linalg.matmul(coefficients, constant(meta['V']), transpose_b=True)
            prediction = (prediction * constant(meta['D_std']) + constant(meta['D_mean'])) / constant(meta['ell_factor'])
        if self.log_preprocess:
            prediction = tf.exp(prediction) + 2 * self.offset
        if self.rescale_by_as and "ln10^{10}A_s" in self.parameter_names:
            index = list(self.parameter_names).index("ln10^{10}A_s")
            prediction = prediction * (tf.exp(data[:, index]) * 1e-10)[:, None]
        if self.galaxy_bias_config and self.galaxy_bias_config.get('enabled', False):
            for kind, exponent in [('quadratic', 2), ('linear', 1)]:
                for start, end, name in self.galaxy_bias_config.get(kind, []):
                    if name in self.parameter_names:
                        bias = data[:, list(self.parameter_names).index(name)] ** exponent
                        prediction = tf.concat([
                            prediction[:, :start],
                            prediction[:, start:end] * bias[:, None],
                            prediction[:, end:],
                        ], axis=1)
    return tape.batch_jacobian(prediction, data).numpy()

def train(self, X, y, learning_rates=[1e-3, 5e-4, 1e-4, 5e-5], *args, **kwargs):
    """Train the model with learning rate scheduling.

    Args:
        X (ndarray): Training input data. Shape (n_samples, n_features).
        y (ndarray): Training target data. Shape (n_samples, n_outputs).
        learning_rates (list, optional): List of learning rates to use
            sequentially. Defaults to [1e-3, 5e-4, 1e-4, 5e-5].
        *args: Additional positional arguments passed to model.fit().
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments passed to model.fit(),
            including 'epochs', 'validation_split', 'batch_size', etc.
    """
    # Scale the training data
    X_scaled = self.input_scaler.transform(X)
    y_scaled = self.output_scaler.transform(y)

    early_stopping = EarlyStopping(
        monitor="val_loss", patience=100, verbose=1, restore_best_weights=True
    )

    for lr in learning_rates:
        print(f"\nTraining with learning rate: {lr}")

        # Compile the model with the current learning rate
        custom_loss = CustomLoss(element_weights=self.rescaling_factor)
        self.model.compile(
            optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lr), loss=custom_loss
        )

        # Get the total number of epochs (this can be adjusted based on your needs)
        total_epochs = kwargs.get("epochs", 200)

        # Wrap the training in a tqdm progress bar
        with tqdm(total=total_epochs, unit="epoch", postfix={}) as pbar:
            # Custom callback to update tqdm progress bar after each epoch and display validation loss (in scientific notation)
            def on_epoch_end(epoch, logs):
                train_loss = logs.get(
                    "loss", 0.0
                )  # Get the training loss from logs
                val_loss = logs.get(
                    "val_loss", 0.0
                )  # Get the validation loss from logs
                pbar.set_postfix(
                    {
                        "train_loss": f"{train_loss:.2e}",
                        "val_loss": f"{val_loss:.2e}",
                    }
                )  # Show losses in scientific notation
                self.train_losses.append(train_loss)
                self.val_losses.append(val_loss)
                pbar.update(1)

            # Train the model with early stopping and tqdm callback
            self.model.fit(
                X_scaled,
                y_scaled,
                callbacks=[
                    early_stopping,
                    LambdaCallback(on_epoch_end=on_epoch_end),
                ],
                verbose=0,  # Turn off default verbose
                *args,
                **kwargs,
            )

        # Optionally save the model at the end of the training cycle
        if self.temp_file is not None:
            self.save(self.temp_file)

def save(self, filename):
    """Save IntegratedModel to disk.

    Saves the Keras model as an HDF5 file and other attributes (scalers,
    PCA, etc.) as a pickle file.

    Args:
        filename (str): Base filename (without suffix) where model will
            be saved. Files will be saved as:
            - {filename}_model.h5 (Keras model)
            - {filename}.pkl (other attributes)
    """
    # Save the Keras model in the .h5 format to handle custom objects like CustomActivation
    self.model.save(filename + "_model.h5")

    # attributes, excluding the model which we've saved separately
    attributes = [
        self.input_scaler,
        self.output_scaler,
        self.offset,
        self.log_preprocess,
        self.pca,
        self.pca_scaler,
        self.parameter_names,
        self.rescaling_factor,
        self.rescale_by_as,
        self.cheby_preprocess,
        self.cheby_meta,
        self.galaxy_bias_config,
    ]

    # Save the remaining attributes to file
    with open(filename + ".pkl", "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump(attributes, f)

    print(f"Model saved to {filename}_model.h5")

def restore(self, filename):
    """Load IntegratedModel from disk.

    Loads the Keras model from HDF5 file and other attributes from
    pickle file. Supports backward compatibility with older model formats.

    Args:
        filename (str): Base filename (without suffix) where model was
            saved. Files should be:
            - {filename}_model.h5 (Keras model)
            - {filename}.pkl (other attributes)
    """
    # Load the Keras model from the .h5 format
    self.model = load_model(
        filename + "_model.h5",
        custom_objects={
            "CustomActivation": CustomActivation,
            "CustomLoss": CustomLoss,
        },
        compile=False,
    )

    # Load the remaining attributes
    with open(filename + ".pkl", "rb") as f:
        attributes = pickle.load(f)

        from UPanda._model_io import decode_attributes
        for key, value in decode_attributes(attributes).items():
            setattr(self, key, value)

    self.scaler_mean_in = self.input_scaler.mean_  # Mean of the features
    self.scaler_scale_in = (
        self.input_scaler.scale_
    )  # Standard deviation of the features

    self.scaler_scale_out = (
        self.output_scaler.scale_
    )  # Standard deviation of the features
    self.scaler_mean_out = (
        self.output_scaler.mean_
    )  # Standard deviation of the features

    print("restore successful")

def create_model(input_dim, hidden_layers=[64, 32], output_dim=1):
    """Create a neural network model with custom activation.

    Args:
        input_dim (int): Number of input features (cosmological parameters).
        hidden_layers (list, optional): List of integers specifying the number
            of units in each hidden layer. Defaults to [64, 32].
        output_dim (int, optional): Number of output dimensions (e.g., number
            of ℓ modes in power spectrum). Defaults to 1.

    Returns:
        Model: Compiled Keras model with custom activation functions.
    """
    inputs = Input(shape=(input_dim,))
    x = inputs

    # Add hidden layers with custom activation
    for units in hidden_layers:
        x = Dense(units)(x)
        x = CustomActivation()(x)

    outputs = Dense(output_dim)(x)

    model = Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs)
    model.compile(
        optimizer="adam", loss="mse"
    )  # Using Mean Squared Error for simplicity
    return model

def create_model_with_dropout(input_dim, hidden_layers, output_dim, dropout_rate=0.1):
    """Create a neural network model with custom activation and dropout.

    Args:
        input_dim (int): Number of input features (cosmological parameters).
        hidden_layers (list, optional): List of integers specifying the number
            of units in each hidden layer. Defaults to [64, 32].
        output_dim (int, optional): Number of output dimensions (e.g., number
            of ℓ modes in power spectrum). Defaults to 1.
        dropout_rate (float, optional): Dropout rate for each hidden layer.
            Defaults to 0.1.

    Returns:
        Model: Compiled Keras model with custom activation functions and dropout.
    """
    inputs = Input(shape=(input_dim,))
    x = inputs
    for units in hidden_layers:
        x = Dense(units)(x)
        x = CustomActivation()(x)
        x = Dropout(dropout_rate)(x)  # Add this!
    outputs = Dense(output_dim)(x)

    model = Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs)
    model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")
    return model

class Provider:
    """Facilitates data sharing between different likelihood components.

    The Provider class handles CMB power spectra sharing for forward modeling
    in lensing likelihoods. It stores CMB spectra computed by one likelihood
    and makes them available to other likelihoods that need them, with
    intelligent caching to avoid redundant computations.

    Attributes:
        cmb_cls (dict): Dictionary containing CMB power spectra ('tt', 'ee', etc.)
        cosmology_params (dict): Cosmological parameters used to compute spectra
        has_cmb_data (bool): Flag indicating whether CMB data is available
        ell_max_cmb (int): Maximum multipole moment ℓ in stored spectra
        stored_units (str): Units of stored data ('FIRASmuK2' by default)
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.cmb_cls = None
        self.cosmology_params = None
        self.has_cmb_data = False
        self.ell_max_cmb = None  # Track the ell range of stored CMB data
        self.stored_units = "FIRASmuK2"  # Track units of stored data

        # Batch processing cache to avoid repeated expensive operations
        self._batch_cache = {}
        self._current_batch_id = None

    def set_Cl(self, cls_dict, params=None):
        """Store CMB power spectra computed by a likelihood.

        Args:
            cls_dict (dict): Dictionary with CMB power spectra. Keys should be
                spectrum types ('tt', 'ee', 'bb', 'te', etc.) and values are
                arrays of power spectrum values. Arrays can be 1D (single spectrum)
                or 2D (batch of spectra with shape (n_samples, n_ell)).
            params (dict, optional): Cosmological parameters used to compute
                these spectra. Defaults to None.
        """
        if not cls_dict:
            raise ValueError("At least one CMB spectrum is required")
        self.cmb_cls = cls_dict
        self.cosmology_params = params
        self.has_cmb_data = True

        # Track ell range (assume all spectra have same shape)
        reference = cls_dict.get("tt", next(iter(cls_dict.values())))
        self.ell_max_cmb = reference.shape[-1] - 1

        # Generate new batch ID when CMB data changes
        self._current_batch_id = id(reference)
        self._batch_cache.clear()  # Clear cache when new data arrives

    def get_Cl(self, ell_factor=False, units="K2"):
        """Retrieve stored CMB power spectra with intelligent batch caching.

        Args:
            ell_factor (bool, optional): Whether to apply the ℓ(ℓ+1)/(2π) factor
                to convert C_ℓ to D_ℓ. Defaults to False.
            units (str, optional): Units for the output spectra. Options are:
                - 'K2': Convert from µK² to K² (divide by 1e12)
                - 'FIRASmuK2': Return in µK² units (no conversion)
                Defaults to 'K2'.

        Returns:
            dict: Dictionary with CMB power spectra. Keys are spectrum types
                ('tt', 'ee', etc.) and values are arrays of power spectrum
                values in the requested units and format.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no CMB data has been set via set_Cl().
        """
        if not self.has_cmb_data:
            raise ValueError(
                "No CMB data available. Please run a CMB likelihood first."
            )

        # Create cache key for this specific request
        cache_key = (ell_factor, units)

        # Check if we already processed this exact request for this batch
        if self._current_batch_id is not None and cache_key in self._batch_cache:
            return self._batch_cache[cache_key]

        # Optimize: Skip unnecessary copy and operations when no processing needed
        if not ell_factor and units == "FIRASmuK2":
            result = (
                self.cmb_cls
            )  # Return directly, no processing needed (already in µK²)
        else:
            # Only copy if we need to modify
            cls_copy = {}
            for key in self.cmb_cls:
                if units == "FIRASmuK2":
                    # CMB likelihoods already send µK² data, so no conversion needed
                    cls_copy[key] = self.cmb_cls[key]
                else:
                    # Convert µK² to K² if K2 units requested
                    cls_copy[key] = self.cmb_cls[key] / 1e12

            # Apply ell factor if requested (this is rarely used for lensing corrections)
            if ell_factor:
                # Handle batch dimensions properly for JAX compatibility
                for key in cls_copy:
                    ells = jnp.arange(cls_copy[key].shape[-1])
                    factor = ells * (ells + 1) / (2 * jnp.pi)
                    cls_copy[key] = cls_copy[key] * factor

            result = cls_copy

        # Cache the result for this batch
        if self._current_batch_id is not None:
            self._batch_cache[cache_key] = result

        return result

def set_Cl(self, cls_dict, params=None):
    """Store CMB power spectra computed by a likelihood.

    Args:
        cls_dict (dict): Dictionary with CMB power spectra. Keys should be
            spectrum types ('tt', 'ee', 'bb', 'te', etc.) and values are
            arrays of power spectrum values. Arrays can be 1D (single spectrum)
            or 2D (batch of spectra with shape (n_samples, n_ell)).
        params (dict, optional): Cosmological parameters used to compute
            these spectra. Defaults to None.
    """
    if not cls_dict:
        raise ValueError("At least one CMB spectrum is required")
    self.cmb_cls = cls_dict
    self.cosmology_params = params
    self.has_cmb_data = True

    # Track ell range (assume all spectra have same shape)
    reference = cls_dict.get("tt", next(iter(cls_dict.values())))
    self.ell_max_cmb = reference.shape[-1] - 1

    # Generate new batch ID when CMB data changes
    self._current_batch_id = id(reference)
    self._batch_cache.clear()  # Clear cache when new data arrives

def get_Cl(self, ell_factor=False, units="K2"):
    """Retrieve stored CMB power spectra with intelligent batch caching.

    Args:
        ell_factor (bool, optional): Whether to apply the ℓ(ℓ+1)/(2π) factor
            to convert C_ℓ to D_ℓ. Defaults to False.
        units (str, optional): Units for the output spectra. Options are:
            - 'K2': Convert from µK² to K² (divide by 1e12)
            - 'FIRASmuK2': Return in µK² units (no conversion)
            Defaults to 'K2'.

    Returns:
        dict: Dictionary with CMB power spectra. Keys are spectrum types
            ('tt', 'ee', etc.) and values are arrays of power spectrum
            values in the requested units and format.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no CMB data has been set via set_Cl().
    """
    if not self.has_cmb_data:
        raise ValueError(
            "No CMB data available. Please run a CMB likelihood first."
        )

    # Create cache key for this specific request
    cache_key = (ell_factor, units)

    # Check if we already processed this exact request for this batch
    if self._current_batch_id is not None and cache_key in self._batch_cache:
        return self._batch_cache[cache_key]

    # Optimize: Skip unnecessary copy and operations when no processing needed
    if not ell_factor and units == "FIRASmuK2":
        result = (
            self.cmb_cls
        )  # Return directly, no processing needed (already in µK²)
    else:
        # Only copy if we need to modify
        cls_copy = {}
        for key in self.cmb_cls:
            if units == "FIRASmuK2":
                # CMB likelihoods already send µK² data, so no conversion needed
                cls_copy[key] = self.cmb_cls[key]
            else:
                # Convert µK² to K² if K2 units requested
                cls_copy[key] = self.cmb_cls[key] / 1e12

        # Apply ell factor if requested (this is rarely used for lensing corrections)
        if ell_factor:
            # Handle batch dimensions properly for JAX compatibility
            for key in cls_copy:
                ells = jnp.arange(cls_copy[key].shape[-1])
                factor = ells * (ells + 1) / (2 * jnp.pi)
                cls_copy[key] = cls_copy[key] * factor

        result = cls_copy

    # Cache the result for this batch
    if self._current_batch_id is not None:
        self._batch_cache[cache_key] = result

    return result

docs.text:
MCMC sampling and parameter space exploration utilities.

This module provides functions for running MCMC sampling and other parameter space exploration methods using various samplers (emcee, nautilus, HMC, ultranest, Adam optimization). It includes utilities for:

  • Prior distribution handling (flat, uniform, Gaussian)
  • Parameter space sampling with various sequences (Sobol, Halton, etc.)
  • MCMC configuration and execution
  • Gaussian prior handling with file-based means/covariances

The module supports both NumPy and JAX backends, with JAX enabling JIT compilation and automatic differentiation for gradient-based optimization and HMC sampling.

def log_gauss(x, mu, cov):
    """
    Compute the log of a Gaussian distribution with mean mu and covariance cov.

    Args:
        x (array): Input values
        mu (array): Mean of the Gaussian
        cov (array): Covariance matrix or scalar variance

    Returns:
        float: Log of the Gaussian PDF
    """
    if ndim(cov) == 2:
        cov = asarray(cov)
    inv_C_gauss = utils.invert_input(
        cov
    )  # inverting the "covariance" which can be a scalar for a single param
    diff_gauss = x - array(mu).T

    if ndim(cov) == 2:  # if matrix
        return -0.5 * (diff_gauss.dot(inv_C_gauss) * diff_gauss).sum(axis=1)
    else:
        return -0.5 * diff_gauss * inv_C_gauss * diff_gauss
